title: Design a CDN
summary: Design a Content Delivery Network for global content distribution.
body:
Design a Content Delivery Network for global content distribution.

## Scenario

Design a CDN that distributes static and dynamic content to users worldwide with minimal latency.

## Requirements

- Global edge server network
- Content caching with intelligent invalidation
- Origin shielding to protect backend
- Support for static files, streaming, and dynamic content
- Real-time analytics on cache hit rates and latency

## Constraints

- Cache hit ratio > 95% for static content
- First byte time < 50ms for cached content
- Purge propagation < 30 seconds globally
- Handle 10M requests/second globally

## What a strong answer covers

- Edge server placement strategy
- Cache hierarchy (edge, regional, origin shield)
- Cache key design and vary headers
- Purge/invalidation mechanism
- DNS-based vs anycast routing

## Reference walkthrough

Two-tier cache hierarchy: edge PoPs in major cities + regional aggregation nodes. Anycast DNS for routing to nearest PoP. Consistent hashing within each PoP for cache distribution. Origin shield as a reverse proxy cache before the origin. Cache keys include URL + relevant Vary headers. Purge via fan-out from control plane to all PoPs. Tiered TTLs: immutable assets (1 year), API responses (configurable). Streaming via chunked transfer with edge buffering.
keyTakeaways: Cache key design and vary headers
